name: advice
notes: EXAMPLE rows, edit for your own work; not measured (state: example). recommend opus = when the deepest model is worth it. A measured row needs class, agent_types, recommend, evidence, samples (>= 30), opus_needed_pct (<= 10), verified; see gt_model_advice.py.

entries.evidence: example: a read-only search over a fixed file set is mostly matching, so a small model usually finds the same files
example: pulling named fields out of a document is a lookup against the text, with a schema to check the result
example: scoring an answer against a written rubric is a bounded comparison, and a second judge can double-check it
example: condensing a known document keeps the main points at the balanced tier, and the source is there to check against
example: a small, well-specified edit with tests to run is routine work at the balanced tier
example: writing a module from a clear spec, with tests that decide whether it is right, is balanced-tier work

example, estimated from this build: Sonnet builders shipped the relax, auto-clear and code-contract work, and independent Opus reviews of presence code on 2026-10-25 (research.md, phase 96 review) found defects the builder missed: a Hello fall-through and an invisible-character check
entries.rule: Sonnet may build security-sensitive code (unlock, presence, secrets, redaction, signing, sandbox), but a deep-tier reviewer must review it before it ships.
entries.when_high_stakes: (1) High stakes if wrong: the work guards access or secrets (unlock, presence, redaction, signing, sandbox), handles untrusted input, or can lose data or race (clears, claims, request files).
entries.when_new_logic: (2) New logic, not a mechanical change: docs, tables, templates, samples, test-only work and grep audits are outside it.
entries.when_tests_pass: (3) Its tests already pass: red code is not reviewed.
entries.when_no_gate: (4) No exhaustive deterministic gate already covers it: where a scanner, a schema or an exact-match test is the check, that is the check.
entries.limit_cluster: Rarity: one deep reviewer per risk cluster per release, never per fork.
entries.limit_fixer: Rarity: a deep fixer only for confirmed HIGH or MEDIUM findings.
entries.limit_differ: Rarity: the reviewer must differ from the builder.
entries.policy_evidence: Estimated, from this build: of about 16 Sonnet forks on 2026-10-27, 2 risk clusters met all four conditions (relax; auto-clear with the CODE contract, batch ledger and 402 mapping). The 2 Opus reviews found 7 MEDIUM defects the builders missed; the other forks met none and got no Opus.

entries.evidence: example, estimated from this build: independent Opus reviews of Sonnet-built presence code found real defects the builder's own tests did not (research.md 2026-10-25, phase 96 review)

entries.evidence: example: races and double actions (session claims, request files, a clear that fires twice) depend on orderings a test rarely covers, and a miss loses data silently
entries.rule: Have the deep tier read the code path end to end and name the interleavings before anything is written.

entries.evidence: example: when the spec must be decided and not followed, a wrong choice is paid for later, so the deeper model's judgement is worth the price
entries.rule: Decide the design with the deep tier; hand the settled spec to Sonnet to build.

entries.evidence: example: a change across many files with invariants between them (this build's manifests, doc counts and hook registry) needs one model to hold all of it
entries.rule: One deep-tier model holds the whole change, because splitting the invariants across builders loses them.

entries.evidence: example: writing tests from a written spec is well-specified work, and running them says at once whether they are right
example: generating a table or a document from material that is already settled is routine work at the balanced tier, and the source is there to check against
